Daily Quiz.question: ১) 'Volpone' is a character created by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Volpone (1605) is a famous play written by Ben Jonson.
Its important character are - Volpone, Mosca, Celia, Bonario, Corvino.

Ben Jonson (1572-1637):
English Stuart dramatist, lyric poet, and literary critic.

His other major plays are-
- Every Man in His Humor (1598),
- The Silent Woman (1609),
- The Alchemist (1610),
- Bartholomew Fair (1614).

Source: Encyclopedia Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Thomas Moore's famous book 'Utopia' was written in-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Thomas Moore (1478-1535) was an Irish writer, poet, and lyricist celebrated for his Irish Melodies.
- 'Utopia' is a work of fiction and socio-political satire by Thomas More, written in Latin and published in 1516.
- The book 'Utopia' (or Kingdom of Nowhere) was originally written in Latin in 1516.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) University Wits were belongs to -
Daily Quiz.exp:
University Wits:
University wits are a group of young dramatists who wrote and performed in London towards the end of the 16th century. 
- They are called University wits because the were the witty students of Cambridge or Oxford University. 
- They upheld the classical ideas, and ridiculed the crudeness of the new English plays. 

University Wits include:
1. Christopher Marlowe - (Cambridge)
2. Robert Greene - (Cambridge)
3. Thomas Nashe - (Cambridge)
4. Thomas Lodge - (Oxford)
5. George Peele- (Oxford)
6. John Lyly - (Oxford)
7. Thomas Kyd (not university-trained)

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Which one was not written by John Donne?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Anatomy of the World
Daily Quiz.exp:
• John Donne is the father of Metaphysical Poet.
• He is called Poet of Love and Religious Poet.
• His famous poems:
- The Good Morrow
- The Sun Rising
- The Canonization
- Twicknam Garden
- For Whom The Bell Tolls
- The Anatomy of the World (book)
- The Frea
- The Ecstasy
- The Funeral etc.

• 'The Excursion' is a poem by William Wordsworth. 

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Who wrote the first English tragedy?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Gorboduc, play by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville that takes as its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain.
- It is the first English tragedy.
- Its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain.
- It is the earliest English tragic play in blank verse.

Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) Which one is considered as the swansong of Shakespeare?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Tempest is considered as the swansong of Shakespeare.
- It is a drama in five acts by William Shakespeare.
- It was first written and performed about 1611 and published in the First Folio of 1623 from an edited transcript.

The major characters are:
- Prospero
- Ferdinand
- Miranda
- Ariel
- Caliban
- Alonso
- Antonio
- Sebastian

Source: Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) 'The Definition of Love' was written by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The poem 'The Definition of Love' was written by Andrew Marvell.

• Andrew Marvell was an English metaphysical poet, satirist and politician.
• His notable works:
- To His Coy Mistress,
- The Definition of Love,
- The Rehearsal Transpros’d
- The Garden etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) ______ translated The Bible into English.
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Wycliffe (1324-1384) translated The Bible into English from Latin.
- He is called the father of English prose.
- He is a famous writer of the Middle English Period.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) Robert Herrick belongs to -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Greatest Cavalier poet is Robert Herrick.
- He is a famous poet of the Caroline Period.
His famous poems are -
- To Daffodils,
- Delight in Disorder,
- The Night Piece of Julia,
- The Slitany to the Holy Spirit.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Who is known as 'Father of English Modern Poetry'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Geoffrey Chaucer is known as 'Father of English Modern Poetry'.

Geoffrey Chaucer:
- Poet Geoffrey Chaucer was born circa 1340, most likely at his parents’ house on Thames Street in London, England.
- The Canterbury Tales became his best known and most acclaimed work.
- He died October 25, 1400, in London, England, and was the first to be buried in Westminster Abbey’s Poet’s Corner.
- Geoffrey Chaucer is considered as the representative poet of 14th Century. 

 Best Works of Chaucer:
- Canterbury Tales
- The nun priest’s Tale.
- The Parliament of Fowls. 
- The legend of good women

Christopher Marlowe - Father English of Tragedy 
Caedmon - Father of English Sacred Songs
Thomas Kyd - Father of English Revenge Tragedy

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) How many Sonnets did William Shakespeare write?
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Shakespeare is the greatest English dramatist.
- He was born on 23 April, 1564 AD and died on 23 April, 1616 AD.
- His Birth place is Stratford Avon. He is often called the bard of Avon.
- Shakespearean period belongs to '1590-1616'.
- He wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
- He was famous for the objective presentation of his deep knowledge about human psychology. 

Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman।

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Beowulf is the Earliest ____ in English literature.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Beowulf is the Earliest Epic in English literature (England).
- It is also the first monument in English literature and written in Anlo-Saxon Period.
- The author of 'Beowulf' is Anonymous.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) ‘The Spanish Tragedy’ is a famous play by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
‘The Spanish Tragedy’ is a famous play by - Thomas kyd.
- It was published in 1584. 
- Thomas kyd is another university wit. 
- He is a famous writer of Elizabethan Age. 

Source: An ABC OF English Literature - Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Who is not a Metaphysical Poet?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Metaphysical poet, any of the poets in 17th-century England who inclined to the personal and intellectual complexity and concentration that is displayed in the poetry of John Donne, the chief of the Metaphysicals.

Other Metaphysical poets are:
- Henry Vaughan,
- Andrew Marvell,
- John Cleveland,
- Abraham Cowley
- George Herbert and
- Richard Crashaw.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Who is the author of 'Euphues'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Euphues (1579), a book thet bears the embryo  of English novel. 
- It was written by  John Lyly.

John Lyly (1554-1606) belongs to the Elizabethan(1558 - 1603) period.
- From the University Wits John Lyly was one of them.
His other famous works-
- Campaspe,
- Sapho and Phao,
- Midas
-  etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) Among them which one is Robert Greene's famous literary work?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Robert Greene was born in July 1558 in Norwich England and died Sept. 3, 1592, London Who was one of the most popular English prose writers of the later 16th century and Shakespeare’s most successful predecessor in blank-verse Romantic comedy.
-He was also one of the first professional writers and among the earliest English autobiographers.
He wrote:
- A Comical History of Alphonsus King of Aragon
- A Looking Glass of London & England.
- Friar Bacon & Frair Bungay.
- James IV

Source: An ABC OF English Literature - Dr. M. Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) Who is the Author of 'Dr. Faustus'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Christopher Marlowe:
- Christopher Marlowe, (baptized Feb. 26, 1564, Canterbury, Kent, Eng.—died May 30, 1593, Deptford, near London)
- He was the greatest dramatist before Shakespeare.
 - Elizabethan poet and Shakespeare’s most important predecessor in English drama, who is noted especially for his establishment of dramatic blank verse. 

Notable Works: 
- Doctor Faustus,
- The Jew of Malta,
- Tamburlaine the Great
- Dido, 
- Queen of Carthage” 
- Edward II

Doctor Faustus. (1592):  
Main Characters: 
- Mephistopheles
- Doctor Faustus
- Lucifer etc are the important  characters of Doctor Faustus. 

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Character ‘King Duncan’ is found in Shakespeare's play -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Character ‘King Duncan' is found in Shakespeare's tragedy Macbeth. 
Macbeth, tragedy in five acts by William Shakespeare.

Its important characters are
- Macbeth,
- Lady Macbeth,
- Duncan,
- Banquo,
- Three Witches.
Macbeth and Banquo are generals serving King Duncan of Scotland.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Who is called the ‘poet of poets’?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Edmund Spenser is called the 'poet of poets'.

Spenser's famous poems are -
- Colin Clouts Come Home Againe
- Mother Hubberd's Tale
- Complaints
- Epithalamion
- The Shepheardes Calender (Poetry Book)
- The The Faerie Queene (Epic)
- Amoretti (Sonnet Collection)

Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) William Shakespeare was born in -
Daily Quiz.exp:
- William Shakespeare was an English dramatist and poet of the sixteenth century.
- He was born on 23 April, 1564 AD and died on 23 April, 1616 AD.
- His Birth place: Stratford-upon-Avon.
- '1590-1616' is called the Shakespearean period.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.
